reviews.reasoning: The petition-taunt-retort reading of 115:1-3 re-derives cleanly against both witnesses: 115:1 opens with a doubled negation addressed to Yahweh, 115:2 voices the nations' taunt about where their God is (web:Ps.115.2), and 115:3 answers it. The catalogue opening at 115:4 with עֲֽ֭צַבֵּיהֶם (oshb:Ps.115.4, 'their idols') is a genuine, independently corroborated seam -- the neighboring decision's own span opens at the same verse. But the rationale's stated contrastive warrant does not hold up against the pointed bytes: it claims v1 AND v3 both carry 'the second-person address to Yahweh' against v4's third-person idol description. Splicing v3 directly from source shows it is itself third-person narration about God, not address to God, so the stated grammatical contrast is only half true (v1 only). See the challenge for the byte evidence; the boundary itself is not in question, only the warrant as stated, and confidence high is not fully earned by that warrant.

challenges.evidence: Spliced MT 115:1 (byte tier, verse_map_oshb.json): לֹ֤א לָ֥נוּ יְהוָ֗ה לֹ֫א לָ֥נוּ כִּֽי לְ֭שִׁמְךָ תֵּ֣ן כָּב֑וֹד עַל חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ עַל אֲמִתֶּֽךָ -- vocative יְהוָ֗ה plus repeated 2ms suffixes (לְ֭שִׁמְךָ 'to your name', חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ 'your lovingkindness', אֲמִתֶּֽךָ 'your truth') is genuine second-person address, matching WEB “Not to us, Yahweh, not to us, but to your name give glory, for your loving kindness, and for your truth's sake” (web:Ps.115.1). Spliced MT 115:3 (byte tier): וֵֽאלֹהֵ֥ינוּ בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כֹּ֭ל אֲשֶׁר חָפֵ֣ץ עָשָֽׂה carries no 2nd-person verb or suffix at all -- וֵֽאלֹהֵ֥ינוּ ('our God', 1cp) with two 3ms perfects (חָפֵ֣ץ 'he desired', עָשָֽׂה 'he did'), matching WEB “But our God is in the heavens. He does whatever he pleases” (web:Ps.115.3) -- a third-person declarative retort, grammatically the same person as 115:4's idol description, not a continuation of 115:1's address. The seam at 115:3|115:4 is independently supported by the referential and generic shift (petition/retort discourse about Yahweh vs. a third-person descriptive idol catalogue) and by the neighboring span's matching start point, but that is a different warrant than the one stated.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently from the pointed bytes rather than the row's own quotations. 115:5-7 do share one colon syntax -- body-part noun followed by a negated finite verb -- six times over three verses (mouth/speak, eyes/see, ears/hear, nose/smell, hands/feel, feet/walk), with 115:7 adding an unpaired third clause on the throat that does not disrupt the pattern the row actually claims. The catalogue's frame verse, 115:4 (“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands.” web:Ps.115.4), and its close, 115:8 (“Those who make them will be like them; yes, everyone who trusts in them.” web:Ps.115.8), both hold at byte tier as quoted. The root behind 115:8's closing participle does recur as the imperative opening 115:9, a real catchword bridge into the next unit, matching the rejected_alternative's account of why the catalogue is not fragmented across three rows. unit_type strophe and confidence high are earned; boundary_evidence_refs, curly-quote/ref pairing, and dual-cite arithmetic all check out (citation_sweep, check_web_quotes, check_refs_mirror all GREEN for this decision).

Re-ran the book-wide skeleton sweeps: בֵּ֣ית אַ֭הֲרֹן ('house of Aaron') returns 4 verses book-wide (115:10, 115:12, 118:3, 135:19) and יִרְאֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה ('those who fear Yahweh') returns 6 verses book-wide (15:4, 22:24, 115:11, 115:13, 118:4, 135:20) -- both match the row's digit-bearing counts exactly. Re-counted the root behind יְ֭בָרֵךְ directly from the spliced bytes rather than trusting the row's count: 115:12 (יְהוָה֮ זְכָרָ֪נוּ יְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ יְ֭בָרֵךְ אֶת בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְ֝בָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת בֵּ֥ית אַהֲרֹֽן) carries three finite forms and 115:13 (יְ֭בָרֵךְ יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַ֝קְּטַנִּ֗ים עִם הַגְּדֹלִֽים) opens with a fourth -- 4 finite occurrences across the two verses, matching the row's digit-bearing claim. That mood shift -- from the imperative trust-triad closing at 115:11 to a narrated, mostly 3rd-person bless-triad opening 115:12 -- is a real, independently verifiable seam driver at 115:11|115:12. 115:15's closing עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ ('who made heaven and earth') does supply the heaven/earth vocabulary 115:16 immediately picks up. The medium confidence is well-calibrated rather than over- or under-stated: the row itself discloses the softer internal seam at 115:13|115:14, where 115:14's jussive continues the bless-vocabulary without a marked speaker or addressee change, and that is an honest concession, not a hedge that should have been resolved. No warrant, count, or quote defect found; boundary_evidence_refs and dual-cite arithmetic check out.

The factual layer of this decision re-derives cleanly. A skeleton sweep of the hallelu-Yah collocation returns 26 verses book-wide; one of those, 115:17 (לֹ֣א הַ֭מֵּתִים יְהַֽלְלוּ יָ֑הּ וְ֝לֹ֗א כָּל יֹרְדֵ֥י דוּמָֽה), carries יְהַֽלְלוּ יָ֑הּ ('they will praise Yah'), an imperfect form, not the imperative liturgical formula, so the curated count is 25 -- matching the disclosure inventory's book-wide total and confirming the row's discrimination between 115:17's and 115:18's forms is byte-accurate, not a rounding claim. 115 is confirmed as an 18-verse, untitled, identity-numbered psalm (no Ps.115.0 title pseudo-verse exists, and web/MT numbering coincide), so 115:18 (וַאֲנַ֤חְנוּ נְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ יָ֗הּ מֵֽעַתָּ֥ה וְעַד עוֹלָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ, closing הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ) is genuinely the psalm's final verse and its sole true hallelu-Yah occurrence. The paseq disclosure at 115:18 and its single-witness tagging pass citation_sweep's inventory check. Where this decision falls short is refs hygiene: device_notes argues that the living/dead antithesis 'closes the psalm's argument begun at v1', and rejected_alternative argues from 'the second-person blessing of v14-15', but boundary_evidence_refs lists only 115:15-115:18 -- 115:1 is not mirrored anywhere in the refs array, and 115:14 is argued without being mirrored (only 115:15 appears). Both verses sit outside this row's own span, so both needed a refs-array entry (check_refs_mirror flags exactly this pair).
